requirements.note: All sections are present in a native inset-grouped list: Account has editable Name/Email fields, and Sign Out confirms with an alert and switches to a signed-out row with Sign In; Reading, Appearance, Library and Notifications are complete, and the master toggle reveals and hides the time picker plus three toggles; Storage shows used space, and Clear Cache confirms with an alert, zeroes the cache and disables itself; About has the version, pushed Privacy and Terms screens, and Rate the App (opens an external store link).
Font, Theme and Sort Order push native checkmark lists with a back button, and the reminder time uses the compact system DatePicker with a wheel popover.
Font and size update the preview live, but the Line Spacing segmented control has no visible effect: Compact, Normal and Relaxed render identically with both Georgia and San Francisco.
Font, size, spacing, theme, sort, every toggle, the reminder time, the cleared cache and the signed-out state all survive a relaunch.
Reset All Settings at the bottom shows a confirmation alert and restores every default, and these persist after a relaunch.

bugs: The Line Spacing control does not change the preview paragraph at all (Compact, Normal and Relaxed are pixel-identical).
The Sepia theme only tints the preview text; the rest of the screen stays white or grey, so Sepia barely looks different from Light.
tells: When scrolled, the inline 'Settings' title sits directly on top of row text (e.g. 'Recommendations' runs into it) with little or no bar material behind it, especially at large text.
Rate the App leaves the app straight away to a blank external screen with the '◀ Settings' back link, with no in-app rating prompt.
Plain rows with no icons and the default blue tint: correct, but generic next to an iOS Settings-style screen.
A.scroll: Native list scrolling: smooth drags, a correct fling with deceleration, rubber-banding past the top, and no blank or popping rows.

requirements.note: All sections are present with Settings-style icon tiles. The Account header shows an avatar, name and email; Sign Out confirms in a native popover dialog and changes the header to a Sign In row that pushes a form. Notifications asks for the real iOS permission and reveals the time picker and three toggles. Storage has a usage bar and a per-category breakdown, and Clear Cache confirms with a dialog and then disables. About has the version, pushed Privacy and Terms pages, and Rate the App.

Font, Theme and Sort push native checkmark lists (each font is shown in its own face, each theme has a swatch), and the time uses the compact system DatePicker. At the largest text size, Line Spacing turns into a pushed picker row.
The preview changes live with font, size (the slider has tick marks) and line spacing, with clearly different leading for Compact and Relaxed, and a caption below sums up the current setting.
Every setting, the reminder time, the signed-out state and the cleared cache all survive a relaunch.
Reset All Settings asks for confirmation and restores all defaults, which persist after a relaunch; the button is disabled while everything is already at the defaults.

tells: Rate the App shows a hand-built sheet with stars and a Submit button instead of the system review prompt.
An orange accent tint across the app (switches, slider, checkmarks): a deliberate brand choice, but not system blue or green.
B.scroll: Native list scrolling: a smooth fling, rubber-banding at the top, a blurred navigation bar over content, and no jumps or blank rows.

why: Both are native grouped-list settings screens that persist and reset correctly. In A the line-spacing control does nothing to the preview and Sepia barely themes the screen, while B's preview responds to all three controls and its themes recolour the whole app. B adds iOS-Settings polish too: icon tiles, a storage usage bar, a real notification permission prompt, and a Reset button that is disabled when everything is already at the defaults.
